recipes.name: Simply Potatoes Cheesy Hash Browns
ingredients_raw: 1 (20 ounce) package Simply Potatoes® Shredded Hash Browns
1 (10.5 ounce) can condensed cream of chicken soup
2 cups Crystal Farms® Shredded Cheddar Cheese

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Coat a 2-quart glass baking dish with nonstick cooking spray.
Combine hash browns, condensed soup, Cheddar cheese, sour cream, onion, and melted butter for casserole in a large bowl; mix well.
Spread into the prepared baking dish.
Stir together corn flakes and melted butter for topping in a small bowl.
Spread evenly over hash brown mixture.
Bake in the preheated oven until tender and golden brown, about 45 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Simply Potatoes Cheesy Hash Browns
raw_recipe.description: These cheesy hash brown potatoes are finished with a buttery cornflake topping for a crunchy casserole that's perfect for potlucks or Sunday brunch.

video.description: If you're looking for an easy and delicious side dish, look no further than the Simply Potatoes Cheesy Hash Browns in this video. This recipe has been a church basement favorite for years and it's easy to see why. Simply Potatoes Shredded Hash Browns are combined with condensed cream of chicken soup, Crystal Farms Shredded Cheddar Cheese, sour cream, onion, and butter to create a creamy and savory casserole. The topping of crushed corn flakes and butter adds a crunchy texture that perfectly complements the cheesy goodness underneath. With just 15 minutes of prep time and 45 minutes of baking time, this dish is perfect for any occasion.

review.reviewBody: I have been using this recipe for years and we love it. Our favorite version though is to use the Simply Potatoes Southwest Style hashbrowns instead of the plain hashbrowns. This gives it a real kick and has tons of flavor. If I use the Southwest style I leave out the onion. I don't usually have cornflakes on hand, so, I generally just use crushed Ritz crackers instead. The potatoes do stay a little firm which we like, but, if you like them softer - I would saute the potatoes a little before mixing everything together.

This is a staple in our house however, I've made two substitutions: I use Cream of Chicken & Mushroom for a little extra flavor and then instead of a corn flake topping, I smash up some seasoned croutons. I sprinkle them on top and then when there's about 15 minutes left of cooking, I drizzle a little melted butter over the top to crisp it up. Delicious!

I used cream of mushroom soup and panko bread crumbs dusted with a bit of paprika and topped with cheese. For the cheese, I used one 8 oz pack of Mexican blend Sargento, which does not have added spice. Instead of onions, I used some minced onions for a subtle flavor that did not interfere with the other flavors. Five stars with the modifications.

I did keep to the recipe except I didn't have cornflakes so I crushed up some Garlic Cheese Croutons. Worked Great! This is good as is or as a base but to get five stars I had to add some onion powder and garlic powder after the first serving. Wow what a difference. For the cheese I used Kraft's Triple Cheddar Mix. This is a great base to use to make your own. Next time, I'll add some more onions, I loved them when I tasted them here. I'll also go ahead and add some more seasoning as listed above, but you really can't go wrong with this base and it is so easy!

We've always called these Aunt Ethel's Escaloped Potatoes as she handed the recipe down to us. I wouldn't change a thing except we bake for 45 minutes, then sprinkle the topping on and continue baking 30 minutes more. They're delicious and a real crowd pleaser! I use store brand, frozen, country style hash browns to save money and they work great. I also take the whole box of corn flakes, crunch them and place pre measured amounts in small zip locks for freezing. Just pull one out of the freezer and it's ready to use, no fuss no muss.

Every year my mother-in-law would make these Cheesy Potatoes for Chriistmas and everyone looked forward to this dish on the holiday meal table.

She did one alteration which made these suburb. Instead of Hash Browns, she used a package of O'Brien Potatoes (the ones that are frozen with the red and green peppers and onions already in the package). MMMMM-good! And easy peazy! 

If you use this idea, omit the onion in the recipe as it's already in the package! This way you do not have to chop up an onion and the square potatoes are absolutely the bomb!!

We also omit the cornflakes as this dish is already perfect and no need for the topping.

I made this for my in laws Christmas dinner it was awesome !! I used Ore Ida shredded potatoes instead of the simply potatoes. I doubled the recipe as I was making it for 15 people. I added 2 cups of taco blend shredded cheese along with the cheddar cheese it calls for. I baked it at 400 degrees for an hour, until you see the golden brown of the potatoes and corn flakes. My family loved it... I will be the one who brings cheesy potatoes every year now. :)

I made this recipe and it was a big hit! I made a double batch because we were having company for Christmas, and it was everyone's favorite dish. I did use the Simply Potatoes Southwest Style Hashbrowns and 1 cup Tillamook medium cheddar, 2 cups Tillamook sharp cheddar, and 1 cup Tillamook colby jack. I did have to add approximately 10 minutes to the bake time, but I think that will vary depending on your oven and what type of baking dish you use. Just do a test taste at the designated time and see if it needs a little more baking. Delish!!!

I love the versatility of this recipe. Instead of using the prepackaged hash, I grated russet potatoes, squeezed out the starch, and sauteed them in a pan with onions and green peppers. I opted out the broth because I didn't have any, threw everything into a pan, and baked it as directed. It still turned out delicious. Would make again, maybe next time with the broth and compare the two.

I used sharp cheddar and added about 1 tsp. of sea salt and sprinkled throughout with black pepper. I also sauteed the onions in about 2 tsp. of butter before adding to the mixture. My son and I loved it!!
Great! Wonderful leftovers. I mixed 1/2 of the shredded cheddar with the batter and the other 1/2 with the topping. I used Ritz crackers in place of corn flakes.

I love this recipe. I added pepper jack cheese and shredded green peppers. I used Everything flavored Ritz Crackers and crushed French fried onions for the topping. Then sprinkled with Everything bagel seasoning. Amazing!
No changes… but only had Campbells cream o mushroom… it worked out great!
I took this dish to a brunch given by my friend. Everyone adored it! The flavors are sensational!
Followed directions and only made one adjustment: Added Salt, Pepper and about 1/2tsp of Onion powder. Turned out perfect and there were no left overs.
Super easy and super yummy! I used heavy cream and chicken base instead of the canned soup. Loved it!!!
I used O'Brien hash browns for a little zing. I also used French fried onions instead of corn flakes. My grandchildren didn't like the peppers but the adults in the crowd sure did! Tasty recipe!
Best dish ever for a brunch!

I need to make these for a work party. I did a test run today and they came out really good. My husband is really picky and he ate the entire serving. I used condensed cheese soup and shredded my own cheese, but otherwise followed the recipe. I think it will be well liked at work.
